author_reading_scope: The complete cited reasoning was inspected from three independent full-text treatments. Jacobson §1 pp. 11–14 and §8 pp. 38–45; Baez PDF pp. 20–23, 27–28, and 31–35; and Petersson §§3–4 and §6 were read. Petersson explicitly omits most proofs, and Jacobson cites rather than proves the characteristic-not-2 H3(O) Jordan identity; neither imported proof replaces the local argument. The local special-product, spin-factor, alternative-octonion, Clifford-interface, and Albert-identity proofs are supplied in the items.

sources.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969

author_read_locators.disposition: The product convention and identity are checked. The local proof displays all four associative products and their matching terms.

author_read_locators.locator: §8, printed pp. 38–45: octonion construction, alternative laws, Hermitian H(O3), and Theorem 5.
author_read_locators.disposition: Terminology and matrix conventions are checked. The source cites the char-not-2 Jordan assertion; its imported proof is not used, and the local exact coordinate certificate supplies it.

sources.title: John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

author_read_locators.locator: PDF pp. 20–23: Jordan identity convention, special matrix examples, and bounded octonionic geometry.
author_read_locators.disposition: The identity and symmetrization conventions are compared; complete local expansions supply the proof.

author_read_locators.locator: PDF pp. 27–28: spin-factor multiplication, Minkowski form, light cone, and Clifford anticommutator normalization.
author_read_locators.disposition: The exact vector/scalar order and plus-Q sign are retained. Local proofs establish the spin identity, square cone, PBW injectivity, and product map.

author_read_locators.locator: PDF pp. 31–35: H3(O) and octonionic projective-plane context.
author_read_locators.disposition: Context only. No classification, determinant, projective-plane, Lie-group, or physics conclusion is used.
